In [[probability theory]], a '''nonlinear expectation''' is a nonlinear generalization of the [[Expected value|expectation]]. Nonlinear expectations are useful in [[utility theory]] as they more closely match human behavior than traditional expectations.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Peng |first=Shige |date=2017 |title=Theory, methods and meaning of nonlinear expectation theory |journal=Scientia Sinica Mathematica |volume=47 |issue=10 |pages=1223–1254 |doi=10.1360/N012016-00209 |s2cid=125094517 |doi-access=free}}</ref> The common use of nonlinear expectations is in assessing risks under uncertainty. Generally, nonlinear expectations are categorized into sub-linear and super-linear expectations dependent on the additive properties of the given sets. Much of the study of nonlinear expectation is attributed to work of mathematicians within the past two decades. 

== Definition ==
A [[functional (mathematics)|functional]] <math>\mathbb{E}: \mathcal{H} \to \mathbb{R}</math> (where <math>\mathcal{H}</math> is a [[vector lattice]] on a given set <math>\Omega</math>) is a nonlinear expectation if it satisfies:<ref name="Peng">{{cite journal |author=Peng |first=Shige |author-link=Shige Peng |year=2006 |title=G–Expectation, G–Brownian Motion and Related Stochastic Calculus of Itô Type |journal=Abel Symposia |publisher=Springer-Verlag |volume=2 |arxiv=math/0601035 |bibcode=2006math......1035P}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Peng |first1=Shige |url=http://sisla06.samsi.info/fmse/pm/ShigePeng.pdf |title=Stochastic Methods in Finance |year=2004 |isbn=978-3-540-22953-7 |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |volume=1856 |pages=165–138 |chapter=Nonlinear Expectations, Nonlinear Evaluations and Risk Measures |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-44644-6_4 |access-date=August 9, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303223024/http://sisla06.samsi.info/fmse/pm/ShigePeng.pdf |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Peng |first=Shige |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-662-59903-7 |title=Nonlinear Expectations and Stochastic Calculus under Uncertainty |publisher=Springer |year=2019 |isbn=978-3-662-59902-0 |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |doi=10.1007/978-3-662-59903-7}}</ref>
# Monotonicity: if <math>X,Y \in \mathcal{H}</math> such that <math>X \geq Y</math> then <math>\mathbb{E}[X] \geq \mathbb{E}[Y]</math>
# Preserving of constants: if <math>c \in \mathbb{R}</math> then <math>\mathbb{E}[c] = c</math>
The complete consideration of the given set, the linear space for the functions given that set, and the nonlinear expectation value is called the nonlinear expectation space.

Often other properties are also desirable, for instance [[convex function|convexity]], [[subadditivity]], [[positive homogeneity]], and translative of constants.<ref name="Peng" /> For a nonlinear expectation to be further classified as a sublinear expectation, the following two conditions must also be met:

# Subadditivity: for <math>X,Y \in \mathcal{H}</math> then <math>\mathbb{E}[X] +  \mathbb{E}[Y] \geq \mathbb{E}[X+Y]</math>
# Positive homogeneity: for <math>\lambda\geq0</math> then <math>\mathbb{E}[\lambda X] =  \lambda \mathbb{E}[X]</math>

For a nonlinear expectation to instead be classified as a superlinear expectation, the subadditivity condition above is instead replaced by the condition:<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Molchanov|first1=Ilya|last2=Mühlemann|first2=Anja|date=2021-01-01|title=Nonlinear expectations of random sets|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s00780-020-00442-3|journal=Finance and Stochastics|language=en|volume=25|issue=1|pages=5–41|doi=10.1007/s00780-020-00442-3 |arxiv=1903.04901 |s2cid=254080636 |issn=1432-1122}}</ref>

# [[Superadditivity]]: for <math>X,Y \in \mathcal{H}</math> then <math>\mathbb{E}[X] +  \mathbb{E}[Y] \leq \mathbb{E}[X+Y]</math>

== Examples ==

* [[Choquet expectation]]: a subadditive or superadditive integral that is used in image processing and behavioral decision theory.
* [[g-expectation]] via nonlinear BSDE's: frequently used to model financial drift uncertainty.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chen |first1=Zengjing |last2=Epstein |first2=Larry |date=2002 |title=Ambiguity, Risk, and Asset Returns in Continuous Time |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/3082003 |journal=Econometrica |volume=70 |issue=4 |pages=1403–1443 |doi=10.1111/1468-0262.00337 |jstor=3082003 |issn=0012-9682}}</ref>
* If <math>\rho</math> is a [[risk measure]] then <math>\mathbb{E}[X] := \rho(-X)</math> defines a nonlinear expectation.
* [[Markov chain|Markov Chains]]: for the prediction of events undergoing model uncertainties.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Nendel|first=Max|date=2021|title=Markov chains under nonlinear expectation|journal=Mathematical Finance|language=en|volume=31|issue=1|pages=474–507|doi=10.1111/mafi.12289|s2cid=52064327 |issn=1467-9965|doi-access=free|arxiv=1803.03695}}</ref>
